items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1957-04-16
items.q: Joe gets Bill Johnson to play bass with him... We finally got Noah Dutrae and Johnny, you see, myself... organized our regular group.

ctx.x: Oh yeah? Garland's New Orleans Jazz Band. Uh-huh. Jazz band, yeah.

Then, uh, Johnny Dodds come in town. We got a hold of Johnny Dodds. Nora Dutre was in the neighborhood. He used to come into Chicago and he'd come sit in with us. So, uh, Boyd H. Williams opened up the, uh, the, opened up this club on 34th Street, uh, Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…
Was it hard to find a piano player at the time?

items.title: 68090_Ed Garland oral history interview
items.q: So he left and he got Bill Johnson. Bill Johnson to play in my place, you know. Take my place.

ctx.x: He said, "Yeah?" He said, "You're going to change your mind." "Oh, no," I said, "I ain't going to change my mind, Joe. I ain't going back to New York." So he kept on. Every day he'd come in and he'd say, "Well, we're leaving Monday. What do you say?" I'd say, "I give you my word, Joe. I'm not going back to New York." "I'm going to stay here." "Okay." So he left and he got Bill Johnson.

items.title: Ed Garland Interview, 1971-04-20
items.q: My name, Johnson was a banjo player. I was on the bass.

ctx.x: Wallace, uh... Geek was a planet man. And we had oil, violin player. My name, Johnson was a banjo player. I was on the bass. Florence Mills, she was singing. You knew Florence Mills, don't you?
I heard of her. All right. I remember.
